key: Booking a whole tempo (circuit) vs using
name: ch08_tempo_vs_shared_auto
alt: A family stuck with a booked tempo that is too small or unavailable, while a shared auto simply squeezes in whatever boxes fit right now.
scene: A split-panel street illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same family shifting house in both halves: a father in his 40s in a checked half-sleeve shirt and a mother in a green cotton salwar kameez, surrounded by cardboard cartons tied with jute rope, a rolled mattress and a steel trunk on the pavement outside a pastel apartment gate. LEFT panel: a small three-wheeled goods tempo, booked for the whole day, is pulling away with only three cartons in its open back, half its bed empty, while most of the boxes still wait on the pavement; a dashed circular arrow shows it must make many slow trips, and the wide road beside it is visibly empty. Above, a small inset bubble shows the father on the phone to a transporter whose shop board has a big red cross over a large truck icon, meaning no big vehicle is available. The father looks frustrated, hand on his forehead. RIGHT panel: a yellow-green shared auto rickshaw has stopped at the same gate; the cheerful driver in a khaki shirt waves the mother in, and two cartons are being squeezed in beside two other passengers already seated, a schoolboy and an old woman with a vegetable bag. A short dotted path shows the auto heading to a fixed auto stand sign at the corner, and one carton has tipped off the roof behind it with a small circular re-send arrow showing it will go on the next auto. Bright morning light, everyday bustle. Labels: "CIRCUIT" at the top of the left panel and "PACKETS" at the top of the right panel.

key: A meeting room booked through the office
name: ch08_meeting_room_overslept
alt: A man who overslept in a booked meeting room wakes after his slot and scribbles on the whiteboard during someone else's presentation.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration of a glass-walled office meeting room told as two moments, left and right, inside the same room with a long table, a grey sofa against the wall, a wall clock and a large whiteboard. Outside the glass door a small booking tablet is mounted on the wall. LEFT moment: a young man in his late 20s in a light blue shirt and lanyard is curled up asleep on the sofa, laptop closed on his chest, mouth open, small Z shapes floating up; the wall clock above him shows a few minutes past two, and the booking tablet by the door shows his name block in the 2 to 3 slot. RIGHT moment: the wall clock now shows twenty past three, and the tablet shows a new block for 3 to 4. A confident woman in her 30s in a maroon kurta and blazer stands at the whiteboard presenting a neat bar chart to two colleagues seated at the table. The man, just woken, hair messy, has walked up beside her and is scribbling his own untidy arrows and words right over her chart with a marker, utterly sure it is still his slot; a thought bubble over him shows a 2 to 3 calendar block with a tick. The woman stops mid-sentence, marker frozen, staring at the mixed-up board; a small red jagged burst marks where the two sets of notes overlap. Bright afternoon office light, comic, awkward mood. Labels: "EXPIRED BOOKING" above the sleeping man's tablet slot and "BOTH WRITES ACCEPTED" above the messy whiteboard.

key: Rules for a school relay race written
name: ch08_relay_race_rulebook
alt: A school sports teacher pins up relay race rules while runners show the three timing assumptions and a runner who rejoins with his lap number written on his hand.
scene: A sunny school sports ground with a red running track, white lane lines and a mango tree in the corner. In the left foreground, a sports teacher in a white tracksuit with a whistle and a clipboard pins a large rulebook sheet onto a wooden notice board on a stand; the sheet shows three small stopwatch icons in a column: a stopwatch with a firm tick, a stopwatch with a tick and a dotted tail, and a stopwatch drawn as a big question mark. On the track to the right, three short vignettes of schoolboys and girls in house-coloured vests and white shorts, each passing a baton: in the first, a girl finishes her lap on time; in the second, a boy has tripped and sits on the track holding his knee while the stopwatch above him runs long; in the third, a boy walks back onto the track scratching his head, looking at his open palm on which a lap number is written in ink, a small zoomed inset bubble showing the palm with "LAP 3". At the far right edge a sly runner takes a shortcut across the grass inside the oval, drawn small, with a little red exclamation badge. There is no referee anywhere on the ground; the umpire's high chair by the finish line is visibly empty. Bright morning light, cheerful school sports day mood. Labels: "SYSTEM MODEL" across the top of the notice board, "STABLE STORAGE" beside the palm inset.
